body:
The sci-fi writings of Jean Giraud meet the magic of Studio Ghibli in Ugo Bienvenu's Arco. It tells of a time-travelling 10-year-old who travels to 2075 from an even further future, befriending a young girl named Iris, along with her robot nanny and baby brother, and getting chased by three doofuses who are the closest thing this film has to villains. In his time, exploring the past is just something everyone gets to do after a certain age. So far ahead is he that he views nigh-sentient robots the way my Gen Alpha relatives view VHS tapes, maybe even gramophone players. With great fascination, I mean.

This movie is a feast for the eyes, and its characters -- while some of them will be dismissed as "rip-offs" of other children's media -- are varying degrees of adorable. The plot, I grant, isn't anything spectacular. But for younger kids, well, this is sure to whisk them away on a journey they won't soon forget.

As for my mandatory Oscars predictions, I strongly doubt it's winning Best Animated Feature (most probably because Disney is snatching it, but I'd like to be optimistic and say that the prize may well be secured by KPop Demon Hunters, which would mark the fourth year in a row that Disney doesn't get it). Hopefully, this doesn't stop it from hitting more screens, even if those screens run Netflix apps. I'm sure the younger generations will fall in love with this one.

Just got out of the theatre from seeing this beautiful little piece. It is not perfect as a whole but it is very touching and perfectly executed for a first. The director successfully creates a signature that is recognizable and new, with his design. Great story great characters. I cried a lot especially towards the end. If you're hesitant to go, do not be and watch it with an open mind and heart.

The writing may not be particularly fantastic, but I do respect the ambitious and colorful direction of what Arco is going for.

It's simple, yet, effective and emotional journey about friendship and childhood loneliness is ambitious and creative. What I really like about this movie is that it doesn't hold it's characters or setting filled with cheesy or animated tropes, it does offer some unique new concepts and interesting themes throughout. I love when animated movies don't follow tropes, but allows some risky emotional and unique takes on the concepts, chararacters and structure. The animation, of course, is colorful, and very different. I'm sure people have said but it does remind me a lot about Studio Ghibli with the model designs and movements.

Alongside with some good music, sound designs, and emotional weight, for the voice performances (keep in mind, I watched this in the English dub), it's tolerable. There are some decent voice performances but some feeling a bit mixed bag. That goes with the writing too, because I do appreciate the story but for the movie being 89 minutes, the structure does feel cramped and I do wish a little bit more was given time to develop more depth and characters.

Overall, it's pretty good. We do need more animated movies like this from smaller scale studios.

Gorgeous movie and very creative with the 2 futures as far as the visuals are concerned. Humans not particularly pretty but there are a few scenes where Arco and Iris' close-ups really get to our hearts.

In terms of the story it took a while to reel me in, and I only became invested in the last third. The ending sealed the deal for me and that's why I gave it 4 stars. It's manipulative but I don't care, such a nice emotional surprise. Everything from the bubble closing onwards just goes really hard on all fronts.

Watched the English dub cause I couldn't find the French version but they say it's pretty good.

Arco is a wonderful movie for the entire family. An Animated feature with multiple themes concerning family and nature.

This film focuses on the importance of humanity's role in a future where machines do most of their work. And nature's state among the changes accruing.

Arco follows the journey of a young boy trying to return to his timeline using time travel. Along his journey he'll encounter Iris, a girl who'll help him, while learning about humanity's future.

As I've mentioned, Arco is a wonderful movie for the entire family. Focuses on many themes while also keeping a light tone for the younger audience.

I highly recommend and encourage parents to watch this movie along their kids, for all to enjoy heartwarming story.
